query: AlCrFeNiSi belongs to a high-entropy-alloy family developed to combine properties that traditional single-principal-element alloys often cannot achieve simultaneously. Earlier research sought stable solid solutions and adjusted HEA compositions to target particular properties, but tradeoffs persisted: the CoCrFeMnNi system has limited wear and corrosion resistance, manganese can promote oxidation and oxide spallation, and cobalt-containing systems raise cost and processability concerns. Conventional bulk fabrication can cause compositional segregation during cooling, whereas mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing techniques can generate residual thermal stresses that impair mechanical performance and increase processing complexity. Given cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock, what single intervention could improve mechanical integrity while limiting segregation, residual stress, and defect formation? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, its causal mechanism, a quantitative or directional outcome relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi, the processing and test boundaries of validity, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Preheating the build plate to 400 °C during laser powder-bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi HEA powder will reduce thermal gradients and cooling rates, leading to more homogeneous microstructures with lower residual stress and fewer defects, thereby improving tensile ductility and overall mechanical integrity relative to an unheated build.
generation.material_initial_state: Gas‐atomized, cobalt‐free AlCrFeNiSi high‐entropy alloy powder (15–45 µm) for laser PBF
generation.intervention: Maintain build plate at 400 °C throughout the PBF‐LB build
generation.conditions: Laser power 200 W, scan speed 800 mm/s, layer thickness 30 µm, argon atmosphere, powder size 15–45 µm, build plate temperature 400 ± 10 °C
generation.structural_mediator: Reduced thermal gradient and slower solidification cooling rate
generation.mechanism: Elevated substrate temperature lowers thermal gradients in the part, enabling greater in‐situ diffusional homogenization during solidification and diminishing solute segregation at dendrite boundaries; the reduced shrinkage mismatch mitigates residual stress and cracking, yielding a more uniform microstructure with fewer porosity and crack‐type defects.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to conventionally built (unheated‐plate) AlCrFeNiSi: ≥20% reduction in average residual stress, ≥30% decrease in measured microsegregation amplitude (elemental concentration variation across dendritic arms), and ≥15% increase in room‐temperature tensile elongation, with yield strength change within ±5%.
generation.baseline: AlCrFeNiSi specimens produced by PBF‐LB with unheated build plate under otherwise identical laser and scanning parameters
generation.boundary: Valid for PBF‐LB builds using 150–250 W laser power, 600–1000 mm/s scan speed, 25–35 µm layer thickness, argon environment at ≤50 ppm O₂, and tensile tests at 20–25 °C; may not hold for other HEA compositions, different AM methods, or much higher/lower preheat temperatures.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate – extrapolated from preheat effects in other Ni-based and Fe-based HEAs; no direct prior data for AlCrFeNiSi

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two sets of AlCrFeNiSi PBF‐LB specimens: one with build‐plate preheat at 400 °C, one without preheat; use identical laser power, scan speed, layer thickness, and atmosphere. After fabrication, measure (1) residual stress via X-ray diffraction, (2) microsegregation via SEM-EDS line scans across dendrites, (3) defect density via X-ray computed tomography, and (4) tensile properties via standard dogbone tests at room temperature.
measurements: Segregation amplitude (% variation in elemental concentration) by SEM-EDS
Tensile elongation (%) and yield strength (MPa) by stress-strain curves
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the preheated‐plate specimens do not simultaneously achieve ≥20% lower average residual stress, ≥30% reduction in segregation amplitude, and ≥15% higher elongation versus the unheated baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
